## What it is

- A Rust dev server that renders `.qmd` to HTML, fast
- Built for one author's blog posts, slides, and books
- Not a general Quarto replacement: HTML only, corpus is the spec

## Three goals

- **Click-to-source**: jump from any block back to its line
- **Block-level updates**: save re-renders only what changed
- **No startup cost**: warm server, warm Jupyter kernel

## How a save flows

- The file watcher notices the change
- The core re-parses and diffs blocks by content-hash id
- Only the changed blocks are pushed over the websocket
- Unchanged blocks (and their live state) are never touched

## Math comes for free

KaTeX renders server-side and ships offline:

$$
p(\theta \mid x) \propto p(x \mid \theta)\, p(\theta)
$$

## Code runs against a warm kernel

```{python}
#| echo: true
sum(n * n for n in range(10))
```

## The same pipeline, three outputs

- Blog posts and books: a scrolling HTML page with a table of contents
- Slides: this deck, split by heading
- All from one block model with stable ids and source positions

## Thanks

- Edit the source and watch this slide update in place
- Double-click any block to jump to its line
